assertions.evidence: The response contains a clearly formatted markdown table starting with '| Scenario | Shipping Method | Destination | Order Value | Cost? |' with multiple rows of shipping scenarios.

assertions.text: Express shipping is split into at least two cases distinguishing the UK free tier (UK, order £50+, free) from the paid tier
assertions.evidence: The table distinguishes Express UK at threshold (£0.00) from Express non-UK at threshold (£9.99): 'Express, at threshold — UK | Express | UK | £50.00 | £0.00' versus 'Express, at threshold — non-UK | Express | {Ireland, EU} | £50.00 | £9.99'

assertions.text: Express rows use value sets to consolidate cases with the same outcome
assertions.evidence: While the below-threshold row consolidates destinations as {UK, Ireland, EU}, the at/above-threshold rows are split by order value rather than consolidated: 'Express, at threshold — UK' and 'Express, above threshold — UK' are separate rows with £50.00 and £75.00 respectively, rather than unified as one row with {£50, £75}. Similarly, non-UK at/above threshold appears as two rows instead of one consolidated row with {£50, £75}.

assertions.text: Overnight UK and Ireland are in one row using a value set ({UK, Ireland})
assertions.evidence: 'Overnight, UK or Ireland | Overnight | {UK, Ireland} | {£10.00, £100.00} | £14.99' shows UK and Ireland grouped in a single row with value set notation.

assertions.text: Standard shipping destination uses a value set covering all options or is blank/absent
assertions.evidence: 'Standard, any destination and order value | Standard | {UK, Ireland, EU} | {£10.00, £100.00} | £3.99' uses a value set covering all destination options.

assertions.text: At least one output column ends with '?'
assertions.evidence: The output column header is 'Cost?' which ends with a question mark.
